NEAR · the short version

NEAR makes new coins. We measured how much it wins back.

8 quick steps. One idea each. Every number is real and you can check it.

  • About 60 seconds

1NEAR makes new coins

Every day, NEAR makes new coins.

89,783new NEAR a day

That adds about 2.5% to the supply each year.

Why it matters: more coins means each coin you hold is a slightly smaller slice. This is called issuance.

New NEAR each day89,783
2The usual view

Most dashboards only count the fee burn.

0.92%

That's how much of the new NEAR gets burnt (destroyed) in fees.

Burnt in fees829 of 89,783 a day

Seen this way, NEAR needs 108× more activity before it destroys as much as it makes.

3What gets missed

But there's a second flow: buybacks.

The NEAR Intents app sends NEAR into a buyback account every day. Count that too:

12.0%

of the new NEAR is won back. That's 13 times what the fee burn alone shows.

Won back each day9,922 buybacks + 829 burn
Distance to break-even, fee burn only
108×
Distance to break-even, burn + buybacks

4Where it goes next

When could NEAR win back everything it makes?

It depends on how fast NEAR Intents grows. Three speeds, all taken from real data:

Fast
+50% a year
2032
Middle
+3% a year
2091
Shrinking
−25% a year
Never

The fastest fix isn't growth. If the buyback took every Intents fee and NEAR cut issuance (a proposal called HSP-029), even the middle speed gets there in about 8 years.

5The honest catch

The catch. We show this too.

  • i
    Bought back isn't burnt.The NEAR sits in an account. Its owners could spend it.
  • ii
    It has dipped.From a peak of 16.5% down to 12.0% now.
  • iii
    One app does most of it.NEAR Intents supplies 92% of what's won back.
  • iv
    The chain got quieter.Daily active accounts are down 70% since February. Most of the drop in app activity is one app (KaiChing) leaving. Intents went the other way: 2.8× more activity.
6So, buy or not?

So what should an investor do?

Our honest call, in four lines:

  • TodayNot yet a supply story. NEAR still mints about 8× what it wins back, and at the median growth rate in the data break-even is in 2091. Don't own NEAR expecting buybacks to offset dilution soon.
  • The betGovernance, not growth. Sending every Intents fee to the buyback (today about 23%) and HSP-029's lower issuance would bring even the base case to about 8 years. Both are votes, not market conditions.
  • Turn more bullish ifHSP-029 clears its veto window (closes 16 Nov 2026), and validators adopt it after the 90-day grace period, or the buyback's share of Intents fees rises toward 50%.
  • Turn bearish ifthe buyback balance keeps falling, payback over 100 epochs drops below 6%, or transfers stop coming from intents.near.
7Ranges, not guesses

We give ranges, not guesses.

One exact number is almost always wrong. So for every forecast we give a range, like "between 7% and 27%".

82%

of the time, the real number landed inside our range when we tested it on past data.

That's the honest bar: tight enough to be useful, wide enough to be right most of the time. Expect the odd miss. A range that is never wrong is too wide to mean anything.
